messages.subject: Re: Installing matR
messages.body_plain:
matR is in its final testing phases -- for now, installation can be accomplished by following the directions on the git repository <https://github.com/MG-RAST/matR>,
copied here for your convenience

Make sure that you have R version 2.15 or later (check with the R.Version() command .

Use the following commands from the R prompt -- Note, this intalls the early-release version:

     currently used in all examples on this forum:

     install.packages("devtools")

     library(devtools)

     install_github(repo="MG-RAST/matR", dependencies=FALSE, ref="early-release")

     library(matR)

     dependencies()

If you experience problems -- please let us know.
The quickest way for us to help, open up an R terminal and paste the following.

msession$debug()

This will generate a log we can use to debug your problem.
Email us through the MG-RAST contact site <http://metagenomics.anl.gov/metagenomics.cgi?page=Contact>, and attach the file.

Note that you should not post the file it generates on this forum.

Cheers
Kevin

messages.subject: Normalized data analysis in matR
messages.body_plain: Is it possible to use normalized data for creating the collections? The manual mentions normalize(), but the option to use entry = "normed.counts" to get the normalized data in the collections seems safer. I cannot see that it's working, though. I've used the normalize function, too, and I know I can get a file of the normalized $raw (or $all for organism annotations) data, but I cannot seem to replace a collection's dataset with these normalized data. This might all be an R issue, so sorry if it's something simple I'm missing. Thanks.
